architectureDecisions: D1 — Facade adds resolveNext(rawRequirement, previousResult) where previousResult is the exact prior facade result {resolution, preObservations, ...}. It validates requirementId equality and uses the delivered defineContextResolution(raw, requirement, previous) chaining check.

D2 — Retriable set R = {BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, SOURCE_FAILURE, DEFERRED}. Non-retriable: STALE, AMBIGUOUS, UNSUPPORTED, CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIABLE, MISSING. If no unresolved evidence has a reason in R, resolveNext throws ProgressionRefused NOTHING_RETRIABLE.

D3 — Remaining budget = requirement.budget - previous.consumed per counter; maxResolutionSteps remaining must be >= 1 else ProgressionRefused STEPS_EXHAUSTED; a COMPLETE previous throws ProgressionRefused ALREADY_COMPLETE.

D4 — Planning uses an operational sub-requirement containing only retriable evidence with budget = remaining; it is passed to retrievalPlanner.execute and catalog validation but never becomes resolution identity. The new resolution is built on the original requirement.

D5 — Items: previous items copied verbatim (same order and content) followed by new items for re-attempted evidence; consumed = previous.consumed + step deltas (exact bytes via the BB-087 two-pass contract method), resolutionSteps = previous + 1.

D6 — Currentness: pre-observe all evidence; any previously resolved evidence whose observation digest differs from previousResult.preObservations throws DurabilityFailure STALE_DURING_RESOLUTION; the post-observation fence is unchanged.

D7 — createPinnedResolver(result) returns {resolve(requirement)} that returns result.resolution when requirementId matches and throws otherwise, so an application can hand a specific step to Core's once-per-call injected port without Core changes.

D8 — Evidence basis: executed probe shows the contract accepts a chained step and rejects steps beyond maxResolutionSteps, while the facade hard-codes step 0 and resolve(rawRequirement, metadata = {}) takes no previous.
implementationSlices: R1 — resolveNext [PR1, PR2]: implement D1-D5 in the facade with tests for chaining, retriable selection, remaining budget and verbatim prior items.
R2 — Refusal + currentness [PR3]: implement D2/D3 refusals and D6 drift fence with tests for ALREADY_COMPLETE, STEPS_EXHAUSTED, NOTHING_RETRIABLE and STALE_DURING_RESOLUTION.
R3 — Pinned resolver + Core [PR1]: implement D7; test passes a step-1 pinned resolver to Core resolveContextRequirementBlocks and asserts one resolve call and the step-1 projection.
R4 — Living truth: export resolveNext-related names, add docs/living/system/oracle/progressive-resolution.md, run test:oracle and npm run verify.

sourceAnchors.match: selected context requirement block needs contextResolver.resolve()

negativeVerificationCases: resolveNext with a previous result for a different requirementId is rejected.

resolveNext on a COMPLETE previous throws ALREADY_COMPLETE; with no remaining steps throws STEPS_EXHAUSTED; with only STALE/AMBIGUOUS/UNSUPPORTED/CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIABLE/MISSING unresolved throws NOTHING_RETRIABLE.
A step whose prior items differ in order or content from the previous resolution fails the verbatim test.
A step adding items for evidence that was already resolved fails the no-hidden-growth test.
Cumulative consumption decreasing or exceeding the requirement budget is impossible and tested.
A previously resolved source whose snapshot changed before the next step throws STALE_DURING_RESOLUTION.
createPinnedResolver given a mismatched requirement throws; Core resolves the pinned block exactly once per call.
Edits to contract, planner, catalog, durability or Core files fail repository scope verification.
